title: Substance objects: singular partitive
summary: Choose singular partitive for an unspecified amount of food or drink.
objectives: Choose singular partitive for an unspecified amount of food or drink.

sections.title: Meaning and pattern
paragraphs: Choose singular partitive for an unspecified amount of food or drink.
A substance can be treated as an amount rather than one whole item. The partitive does not tell you an exact quantity. A food word is not automatically partitive in every sentence.
The Finnish verb and complete noun alternatives are provided. Decide which case fits the stated amount.
keyPoints: An unspecified amount of a substance uses singular partitive as the object, the thing the action concerns.

steps: An unspecified amount of a substance uses singular partitive as the object, the thing the action concerns.
Juon means “I drink” and works as the verb. juon comes from juoda: juo- + -n.
kahvia means “coffee” and works as the singular partitive noun used as the object of the action. This i-word keeps i: kahvi + a = kahvia. The back vowel a determines the ending.
An unspecified amount of a substance uses singular partitive as the object, the thing the action concerns.
Juon means “I drink” and works as the verb. juon comes from juoda: juo- + -n.
maitoa means “milk” and works as the singular partitive noun used as the object of the action. Keep maito and add -a: maito + a = maitoa.
An unspecified amount of a substance uses singular partitive as the object, the thing the action concerns.
Syön means “I eat” and works as the verb. syön comes from syödä: syö- + -n.
leipää means “bread” and works as the singular partitive noun used as the object of the action. Keep the final ä and add another ä: leipä + ä = leipää.
An unspecified amount of a substance uses singular partitive as the object, the thing the action concerns.
Syön means “I eat” and works as the verb. syön comes from syödä: syö- + -n.
juustoa means “cheese” and works as the singular partitive noun used as the object of the action. Keep juusto and add -a: juusto + a = juustoa.

commonMistakes: Do not assume every food word always uses partitive.
Do not change the supplied verb when choosing the noun form.
